initial_query: Analyze liability limitations across all vendor contracts

report_sections.title: Executive Summary
report_sections.content: This analysis reviews liability limitation clauses across 15 vendor contracts in the SRC corpus. The review identifies three distinct liability cap structures and highlights jurisdictional variations.

report_sections.title: Key Findings
report_sections.content:
1. Standard Cap Structure: Most contracts (10 of 15) limit liability to 12 months of fees paid under the agreement. This is consistent with industry practice for B2B SaaS contracts.

2. Enhanced Caps for High-Risk Services: Three contracts (SRC-DOC-205, SRC-DOC-207, SRC-DOC-210) include higher caps (24 months of fees) for services involving sensitive data processing.

3. Uncapped Liability Categories: All contracts exclude certain obligations from liability caps, including indemnification for IP infringement, data breaches, and willful misconduct.

report_sections.title: Recommendations
report_sections.content: Based on the analysis, we recommend standardizing liability cap language across all vendor contracts. The 12-month standard cap provides adequate protection while remaining commercially reasonable. For high-risk services, the 24-month enhanced cap should be consistently applied.
